## TWEE EN VEERTIGSTE HOOFDSTUK.
### *Het Overſpels-kruid.*

**D** *aun falawar wil ook uit de maagfchap van Conyza zyn, dog aan wasdom komt het met den ſmalblaadigen Tabak over een. Het ſchiet op als een heeſter met een houtagtige ſtam, zes en agt voeten hoog, die zig in veele ronde en ſtyve zydetakken verdeeld, zomtyds zeer wyd uitgebreid als een formeel boompje.*
*De bladeren ſtaan enkeld, en na vooren toe digt op malkander op langagtige ſteelen, den ſmalblaadige Tabak gelyk, dog kleinder, agter en vooren toegeſpitst, met evene kanten, zeven en negen duimen lang, vier en vyf breed, dog de voorſte aan de oude ſtokken zyn kleinder, boven hoog-groen, dog doods, van onderen wat graauw, ruig in 't aantaſten, en daar en boven met een kleeverig zand bestrooit, gelyk ook 't geheele kruid is, als men ze wryft, van een zwaaren reuk, ſchier als de vrugten van Bate die ſtinken, de ſmaak is niet zonderlyk ſcherp, hoewel wat bitter en doordringende.*
*De bovenſte ſteelen dragen veele doods-groene en zandige knopjes by een gehoopt in een dolle, waar uit werden kleine vuil-witte bloempjes, met een groen middel-ribbetje van vyf overeind ſtaande, daar na agterwaarts gebooge blaadjes gemaakt, in een diep geboord kelkje, in de midden met korte draadjes, en daar op veele geele noppen met nog een langer ſtyltje bloed, na dezelven volgen ronde vrugten als Piſtool-kogels mede zandig, eerſt groen, daar na bleek-geel, binnen vol kleine platte korrels in een fappig merg.*
*De bladeren hebben tot een byzonder merkteken, dog meeſt de oude, dat zy de eene zyde agter aan den ſteel langer hebben als de andere. De wortel is wyd verſpreid, en houtagtig.*
*Naam. In 't Latyn Adulterina; ſive Folium zelotypiæ; of eigentlyk Remedium contra noxam adulterii; in 't Maleits Daun falawar met dezelve beduidenisſe; in 't Amboins Ayloun puti. Salawar nu noemen de Maleiers het kwaad, dat de kleine kinderen over komt, als een van de ouders, inzonderheid de vader zig in overſpel verloopt, of immers de moeder ſuſpicii daar toe geeft, waar door de jaloeze moeder ontſteeken zynde met haar zog, zoo ik gisſe, het kind ook ontſtelt, want de vrouwtjes maken 't malkanderen zoo wys, dat de ſmettinge door den vader by andere vrouwen bebaald, aan de zuigende kinderen overgaat, waar door dezelve ongedaan, mager en ziekelyk werden, maar zy willen de mannen niet wyzer maken, dat diergelyke fouten by haar begaan, baare kinderen ſchadelyk zy.*
*Is dat niet een fraay geloove, 't welk ik vaſtelyk ſuſtineer zyn oorſpronk te hebben van een zeker geeft Salambar genoemd, den welken de Arabiers, en Mooren zeggen een duivel te zyn, wiens werk en officie anders niet is dan haat en jaloezy tusſen getrouwde lieden te verwekken. En hoe heeft hy dit beter konnen doen, als de vrouwen wys te maken, dat wanneer baare kinderen by geval mager en ziekelyk werden, dat dan den vader moet buiten de pot gepiſt hebben. Dan gaat het eerſt aan een razen en tieren, en dan loopt men ſtraaks na een oude Toverhexe, die het kind met berooking en beleeingen van deze infectie bevryd.*
*Hier om mag men dit kruid Herba zelotypiæ noemen, en den voorſchreeven Geeſt Salambar, daemon zelotypiae. Anders noemd men bet met beter reden ook Tabaco utan, of wilden Tabak, welke naam dit kruid meer eigen is, dan de voorgaande vierde ſoorte van Sombong.*
*Plaats. Het wast op magere gronden, ongebouwde plaat-zen in 't veld, en agter de huizen van de Negorijen.*

## CHAPTER FORTY-TWO.
### The Adulteress Herb. Daun falawar.

**D**aun falawar also seems related to the Conyza, yet in its manner of growth it resembles narrow-leaved Tobacco. It grows like a shrub with a woody stem, six or eight feet high, and divides into many round and firm side branches, sometimes spreading as wide as a small tree.
The leaves are solitary and clustered at the top, sitting on rather long stalks; they are similar to narrow-leaved Tobacco but smaller, pointed at both ends, with even edges, seven to nine inches long and four to five wide. However, the upper leaves on older stems are smaller. They are deep green above but not shiny, and ash-colored below, rough to the touch and moreover viscous as if sprinkled with sand—as is the whole herb. If crushed, they give off a heavy odor much like the stinking Bate fruit <note>original: "fructus Bate"; likely referring to a local fruit known for a pungent, perhaps cadaverous, smell</note>; the taste is not particularly sharp, though it is bitter and penetrating.
The upper stalks bear many dull green and sandy little heads clustered together like an umbrella, which open into small, dirty white flowers. These sit in a bearded cup <note>original: "calici barbato"; the calyx of the flower</note> and consist of a green pistil and five petals, which are at first erect and then bent backward, with short filaments bearing yellow anthers. After these, round fruits grow out, resembling the balls of a pistol or small handgun, also sandy, first green and then yellowish, filled inside with flat grains hidden in a juicy pith.
The leaves have a peculiar characteristic, especially the older ones, in that one half of the leaf at the stalk is longer than the other. The root is widely spread and woody.
*Name.* In Latin, *Adulterina* <note>original: "Adulterina"; meaning 'The Adulteress'</note>, or *Folium zelotypiae* <note>original: "Leaf of Jealousy"</note>, or more properly, a remedy against the harm of adultery. In Malay, *Daun salawar* has the same meaning, and in Amboinese, *Ayloun puti*. Now, the Malays use the term *Salawar* for an affliction that comes upon young children or infants when one of the parents, especially the father, is guilty of adultery, or at least gives the wife cause for suspicion of that crime. Because of this, the suspicious and angry mother "adulterates" her milk, and by giving it to the infant, as I believe, causes harm. For the common women convince one another that the infection contracted by the parent with other women passes to the nursing children, whereby they become emaciated and languid. However, they do not convince the men that such faults committed by them are harmful to their children.
Is this not a fine faith, or rather a credulity, which I firmly believe arose from a certain spirit called *Salambar*, whom the Arabs and Ethiopians say is a certain devil whose only duty and office is to stir up and cause hatred and suspicion between married people? How could he accomplish this better than by persuading the women that if their infants happen to grow thin and sickly, the father must have been unfaithful? <note>Dutch original: "buiten de pot gepist"; literally "pissed outside the pot," a common idiom for cheating or adultery</note> From this, quarrels and anger are stirred up, whereupon they immediately seek out witches who free the infant from this infection with incantations and fumigations.
And for this reason, this herb can be called the Herb of Jealousy, and that spirit or devil *Salambar*, the demon of jealousy. Otherwise, it is called with better reason *Tabaco utan* or Wild Tobacco, which name is more proper to this herb than to the preceding fourth species of *Sombong*.
*Location.* It grows on thin soils, in uncultivated places, in fields, and behind the houses of the villages <term>Negorijen: native villages or settlements in the Dutch East Indies</term>.

## FORTY-SECOND CHAPTER.
### *The Adultery Herb.*

**D** *aun falawar also belongs to the family of Conyza, yet in its manner of growth it agrees with the narrow-leaved Tobacco. It shoots up as a shrub with a woody stem, six and eight feet high, which divides into many round and stiff side branches, sometimes very widely spread like a formal little tree.*
*The leaves stand singly, and toward the front they are close together on somewhat long stalks, like the narrow-leaved Tobacco, though smaller, pointed at the back and front, with even edges, seven and nine inches long, four and five wide, though the front ones on the old stalks are smaller. They are deep green above, but dull, somewhat gray from beneath, rough to the touch, and moreover sprinkled with a sticky sand, just as the whole herb is. When one rubs them, they have a heavy smell, almost like the fruits of Bate that stink; the taste is not particularly sharp, although somewhat bitter and penetrating.*
*The uppermost stalks bear many dull green and sandy buds heaped together in a cluster, from which are made small dirty-white flowers, with a green mid-rib, of five standing upright, then backward-bent petals, in a deep-bored little cup. In the middle are short threads, and upon them many yellow nubs with another longer style; after these follow round fruits like pistol balls, also sandy, first green, thereafter pale yellow, inside full of small flat grains in a juicy pith.*
*The leaves have as a particular mark, though mostly the old ones, that they have one side at the back of the stalk longer than the other. The root is widely spread and woody.*
*Name. In Latin Adulterina; or Leaf of Jealousy; or properly Remedy against the harm of adultery; in Malay Daun salawar with the same meaning; in Amboinese Ayloun puti. Salawar is what the Malays call the evil that happens to small children when one of the parents, especially the father, strays into adultery, or at least gives the mother suspicion thereof. Through this, the jealous mother being inflamed, she also upsets the child with her milk, as I guess. For the women make each other so wise as to believe that the infection caught by the father from other women passes to the nursing children, whereby they become undone, thin, and sickly. But they do not want to make the men any wiser, that such faults committed by them are harmful to their children.*
*Is that not a fine belief, which I firmly maintain has its origin from a certain spirit called Salambar, whom the Arabs and Moors say is a devil, whose work and office is nothing other than to provoke hatred and jealousy between married people. And how could he have done this better than to make the women believe that when their children by chance become thin and sickly, the father must have "pissed outside the pot" <note>original: "buiten de pot gepist"; unfaithful</note>. Then it first comes to a raging and storming, and then one runs immediately to an old witch, who frees the child from this infection with fumigation and incantations.*
*For this reason, one may call this herb the Herb of Jealousy, and the aforementioned Spirit Salambar, the demon of jealousy. Otherwise, one calls it with better reason also Tabaco utan, or wild Tobacco, which name is more proper to this herb than the preceding fourth sort of Sombong.*
*Place. It grows on lean soils, uncultivated places in the field, and behind the houses of the villages.*

靛青加脂為蓮青。再加上粉為藕合。濃綠加墨為油綠。淡綠加赭為蒼綠。藤黃合硃為金黃。粉紅加赭為肉紅。加硃為銀紅。脂加硃為殷紅。脂加黃為金黃。五色相配。變化無窮。無益花鳥者不及備載。

<meta>This page continues the technical instructions on pigment preparation and color theory, specifically focusing on the ratios for mixing various shades of green and the versatile applications of Ochre.</meta>

<header>Manual of Painting, Volume One</header>
<page-num>Twenty-five</page-num>

**Deep Green** <note>original: 深綠 (shenlü)</note>. Seven parts **Indigo** to three parts **Gamboge** <note>original: 藤黃 (tenghuang); a traditional mustard-yellow pigment derived from tree resin</note>. This is suitable for the leaves of camellias, laurels, and orange trees. For outlining and shading, use pure indigo.

**Blue-Green** <note>original: 青綠 (qinglü)</note>. Equal parts indigo and gamboge. This is suitable for all types of thick, lush leaves. For outlining and shading, use the **Deep Green** mixture described above.

**Tender Green** <note>original: 嫩綠 (nenlü)</note>. Three parts indigo to seven parts gamboge. This is suitable for the young leaves of all woody plants. For herbaceous flowers, one should add even more [yellow]. 

There is also a variety for the **youngest leaves**, which uses only gamboge for the base. Use **Rouge** <note>original: 胭脂 (yanzhi); a red pigment made from safflower or cochineal</note> for the shading and the outlines, then back the silk or paper with green powder.

## Ochre
<term>Ochre</term> <note>original: 赭石 (zheshi); a mineral pigment ranging from golden-brown to deep reddish-brown</note>

<margin>Mixed with yellow, it creates **Areca-nut Color** <note>original: 檳榔色 (binglang se)</note>, which is used for chrysanthemum petals.</margin>
<margin>Mixed with green, it creates **Gray-Green** <note>original: 蒼綠色 (canglü se)</note>, used for the buds and stalks of wintersweet and okra, as well as the tender branches of trees.</margin>
<margin>Mixed with <unclear>X</unclear> for the old stems of herbaceous flowers.</margin>
<margin>Mixed with vermilion, it creates **Old Red** <note>original: 老紅 (laohong)</note>, used for chrysanthemum petals.</margin>
<margin>Mixed with ink, it creates **Iron Color** <note>original: 鐵色 (tiese)</note>, used for tree roots and trunks.</margin>
<margin>Mixed with rouge and ink, it creates **Dark Sauce Color** <note>original: 醬色 (jiangse)</note>, used for the stalks of begonias and apricot blossoms.</margin>

One must select mineral pieces that are vibrant and moist in appearance, with a texture that is neither too hard nor too soft. Grind them finely in a sand mortar. Decant the "white water" <note>the thin, cloudy liquid that rises to the top</note> from the surface and discard the coarse dregs at the bottom. Mix the fine sediment with glue and simmer until dry. This pigment is used for old branches, withered leaves, buds, and stalks. It is a color that harmonizes with all others.

---

## Mixing Various Colors

The various shades of green were previously detailed under the sections for **Indigo** and **Gamboge**. Several mixtures for **Ochre** were also just listed. Any remaining combinations are recorded here for your convenience in color matching.

**Indigo** plus **Rouge** makes **Lotus Purple** <note>original: 蓮青 (lianqing)</note>. 
Adding **White Powder** to this makes **Lotus Root Color** <note>original: 藕合 (ouhe)</note>. 
**Concentrated Green** plus **Ink** makes **Oil Green** <note>original: 油綠 (youlü)</note>. 
**Pale Green** plus **Ochre** makes **Gray-Green**. 
**Gamboge** mixed with **Vermilion** <note>original: 硃 (zhu)</note> makes **Golden Yellow**. 
**Pink** <note>original: 粉紅 (fenhong)</note> plus **Ochre** makes **Flesh Pink**. 
Adding **Vermilion** to pink makes **Silver Red**. 
**Rouge** plus **Vermilion** makes **Deep Red** <note>original: 殷紅 (yanhong)</note>. 
**Rouge** plus **Yellow** makes **Golden Yellow**. 

When these five primary colors are combined, the variations are infinite. Colors that do not benefit the painting of flowers and birds are not recorded here.

<summary>This page provides specific mixing ratios for different shades of green and details the multifaceted uses of Ochre in depicting botanical details. It concludes with a comprehensive color-mixing guide for various hues used in traditional flower-and-bird painting.</summary>
<keywords>pigment mixing, Indigo, Gamboge, Ochre, botanical painting, color theory, Chinese painting techniques, Rouge, Vermilion</keywords>

# Treatise on Armament Technology, Volume 96: Critique of Military Tactics, Supplement Part 1

...it is possible. In such places, one can use the few to attack the many. Great forests and lush grasses are where one sets an **ambush**. Open plains and sprawling fields are where **cavalry** can support one another. Where vegetation and obstacles provide cover, **foot soldiers** can engage in combat. On the open outskirts where there is room to maneuver, allowing for both advance and retreat, one should use **long halberds** <term>Ji: a traditional Chinese polearm combining a spearhead with a side blade</term> to face the enemy.

When crossing water or spanning great distances, or when utilizing differences in elevation where the enemy cannot get close, one should use **long-range crossbows** to face them. Where rocky cliffs provide concealment and narrow paths wind and turn, one should use **swords and bucklers** to face the enemy. In marshes of reeds and rushes where the branches and leaves obscure the view, one should use **spears and iron-staves** <term>Ge and Ting: the Ge is a dagger-axe, while the Ting is an iron-pointed staff or short spear</term> to face the enemy. These are all dictated by the **natural character of the terrain**.

Someone asked: "Suppose within the stockades and camps, the three armies are already at rest. If the enemy takes advantage of a lapse to launch a sudden assault and attack, what should be done at such a moment?"

**Dong** <note>Referring to Xu Dong, the author of the *Tiger Seal Scripture* (Huqian Jing)</note> replied: "Station the brave in the front and hide the timid in the rear. In a moment of sudden crisis, if the timid are forcibly driven to the front, they will surely blunt your own momentum and break the edge of your elite forces. It is better to keep them concealed."

The questioner asked: "In such a moment, how can one find the time—"

All heavenly beings, humans, and <term>asuras</term> in the world revere me; they should also revere this profound <term>Prajnaparamita</term>. Therefore, it is good. I use immeasurable, skillful means to entrust this profound <term>Prajnaparamita</term> sutra to you. You must accept and uphold it. Do not let it be forgotten. I now take this profound <term>Prajnaparamita</term> and, before the great assembly of heavenly beings, humans, and <term>asuras</term>, entrust it to you. You should receive and uphold it in your heart; do not let it be forgotten. 

It is good. Now, with sincere words, I tell you, all good sons and daughters of pure faith: if you wish not to abandon the treasures of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha, or the supreme Bodhi <note>enlightenment</note> of the Buddhas of the three times, you must not abandon this profound <term>Prajnaparamita</term>. This is what we Buddhas teach and instruct our disciples. You should know that if there are those who joyfully listen to, accept, uphold, read, recite, and become completely fluent in the <term>Prajnaparamita</term>, contemplating it according to the truth, writing it down, explaining it, and bestowing it—they are realizing supreme, equal, and perfect enlightenment. Because the <term>Prajnaparamita</term> is the source from which the supreme enlightenment of all Buddhas is born, one should rejoice. 

If Bodhisattvas, Great Beings, wish to attain enlightenment, they must be diligent and exert themselves in studying the <term>Prajnaparamita</term>. Why? Because the profound <term>Prajnaparamita</term> is the mother of all Bodhisattvas, Great Beings; it enables Bodhisattvas to swiftly attain enlightenment. You should know that if Bodhisattvas desire to protect this <term>Prajnaparamita</term> at the time of their passing, they are protecting the omniscience of the Buddhas of the three times, and they are also protecting the infinite Dharma-treasury <note>the repository of all Buddhist teachings</note> of the Buddhas of the three times. 

You should know that if Bodhisattvas diligently study the six <term>paramitas</term> <gloss>perfections</gloss>, they will swiftly attain supreme, equal, and perfect enlightenment. Therefore, you should rejoice and not let the <term>Prajnaparamita</term> be forgotten. Why would I ask you to accept and uphold it and not let it be forgotten? Because these six <term>paramitas</term> are the infinite Dharma-treasury of the Buddhas of the three times. You should know that the essential Dharma taught by the Buddhas and World-Honored Ones of the ten directions and three times all flow out from this infinite Dharma-treasury of the six <term>paramitas</term>. The Buddhas of the ten directions and three times, along with their disciples, all rely on this infinite Dharma-treasury to diligently study and practice; having done so, they will attain supreme enlightenment and enter the ultimate...

<meta>This page continues the technical discussion of monastic discipline (Vinaya), specifically focusing on the rules governing the Kaṭhina period—a time after the summer retreat when monks are granted special privileges regarding their robes.</meta>

# Pelliot chinois 3113

Regarding the equipment for luxury robes and the rules for **not losing the privilege of the robe** <note>During the Kaṭhina period, monks are permitted to be separated from their three robes without committing an offense. "Losing the robe" refers to the expiration of this special privilege.</note>. In the midst of water, if a few people draw water, even at night; or as some say, within the constant flow of a river, one must not stop or bury [the boundary]. 

The markers for the boundary are determined by eight trees, seven intervals, and sixty-two steps. These serve to partition the surface. If we discuss the **Pavāraṇā sheds** <note>Pavāraṇā (self-correction) is the ceremony held at the end of the rainy season retreat; "sheds" refers to the temporary structures or designated areas for this rite.</note>, there are fifteen types:

1.  Where the Sangha is absent, and the two times are not listed.
2.  Fruit trees, where the trees are interconnected; it is permitted for someone to guard them, and the interior is restricted by a screen.
3.  Where gaps are established by ten fingers' width <note>A traditional unit of measurement in the Vinaya.</note>, specifically screened; if in a place with fruit, it must be treated four times over.
4.  Where the establishment is constant.
5.  Where the middle is not yet reached.
6.  Where practitioners walk a great distance and return; the interior is double-screened. 
7.  If the area is insufficient, six types of boundaries are listed; the boundary is for the time of return and the location.
8.  A wooden boundary; "middle" refers to the markers of the fields where one stays.
9.  A screened boundary; after the screening, the time is fixed to the location.
10. A room boundary; a place where many scattered repairs are made.
11. A house boundary; where numbers are stored in six locations.
12. **An island boundary**; involving lakes or rivers; if one studies there, even if the time passes, one does not lose the robe privilege.
13. **A well boundary**; involving secret paths and irrigation; if one stays overnight and places their robe there, they do not lose the privilege during their stay.
14. [Missing in original sequence]
15. A boundary where there are many people, or a small sea, or the sands and stones of the south. <gloss>Bulrushes</gloss> A path through the surging waves. These two boundaries are established by name.

There are two types of "reaches" <note>likely referring to coastal or river reaches</note> at the boundary's edge. When people of three types arrive, seeking a common residence, they establish the **Kaushambi** <note>original: 憍薩彌 (Qiāosàmí). This likely refers to a legal precedent or specific tradition regarding the Kaṭhina robe from the city of Kosambi.</note> foundation. If there are people within the boundary together with the monastery, or if they are outside the boundary, or if they are not in order, the boundary may be large or slightly different. If they merge into one later, it follows the Kaushambi extension.

If within a large boundary there is a monastery, and the outside of the boundary is not confused and does not flow together, then later scriptures mention villages like Tangmai and Yicun. 

According to the **Vinaya** <term>Vinaya: The code of monastic discipline.</term>, if there is no established Law <note>Dharma-rule</note>, and one is within a village, the robe is protected. Because this matter is not yet according to the Law, the "Path" is considered the Law. It does not matter if there is a village or not; the Law of the Vinaya flows through. If a village existed first, one follows the Law and later establishes the unified "Golden Cloister." 

If an outsider has not yet entered, the rule states that the head of the teaching is not within the boundary. If one departs from the village, a new boundary path is made. If there is a village marker, and the village acts improperly, it is called an "Empty Kaṭhina." According to the meaning, one seeks the Kaṭhina through the village marker. If it is not a Kaṭhina, the robes are not yet relinquished. 

If a person enters and the robe is not under the Kaṭhina boundary, and they stay within the riverbed, the robes accumulate merit to the limits of the village. If the village is gone, or if the markers of the teaching are not established, it is not a robe boundary. This is fixed. Therefore, next we remove the robes and the deep Kaṭhina teachings. This is the ultimate discussion.

**Question:** When there is a village, can one borrow it first? How is the Kaṭhina removed?
**Answer:** According to the Vinaya, it does not matter if it exists or not. One first observes the surroundings, then relinquishes the robe. If the relinquishing of the robe follows the Law, one can first establish the Kaṭhina markers. If one speaks of the method of removal, and says it follows the previous village markers, the current Law is not the Kaṭhina. 

Regarding the **Taking of the Kaṭhina**: The Vinaya says if a village existed previously, first observe the surroundings and rely on the previous clothing. If one takes the Kaṭhina outside the boundary, that is the "True Kaṭhina." Because it is a new Law, it is called the "Path Kaṭhina Boundary." If it is doubled, it is a new name and does not depend on the boundary. Among those who follow the Law, the witnesses manage the matter. In harmony, they follow the Law to modify and fix the robes. If the various parts of the body are too short or mismatched, it is decided by the Law.

Between the Kaṭhina and the village boundaries: one follows the markers of the village. The village boundary is the Kaṭhina boundary. Furthermore, when many people divide the merit, they obtain the boundary. Regarding the village, if one enters the village against the flow: 
According to the Vinaya, at the very beginning, there is a gap of one Kaṭhina. The "Faithful Kaṭhina" robe follows the Law. Furthermore, if one acts as a boundary companion, and the place fully has the Kaṭhina, the boundary is within the path. 

**Question:** Regarding staying overnight with the Kaṭhina robe? 
**Answer:** One follows the Law. If there is a gap, one follows the Law. Whether it is Kaṭhina or not, if it is by a river or stream, and the boundary is scattered or the boundaries of the "Color Limit" are fallen, and people do not know the markers: if there are houses in the middle, the robe rule says one must know the method of steps. Whether it is Kaṭhina or not is determined by the "Kaṭhina of Faith." One follows the twelve steps and relies on the gap. If this single gap of the robe is not a village, the markers are few. One can name it the "Kaṭhina of Faith." If the houses are not mismatched, they share the same nature.

There are three types of "Staff Paths": 
1. Utilizing the robe boundary and releasing many.
4. The village path in two places, with Kaṭhina markers appearing to be exhausted.

One checks the numbers and followers, then later determines the **Natural Kaṭhina of Faith**. Those who are not following the Law refuse the boundary and the restricted path of the Kaṭhina. Using the name of the path to differentiate a single interval, the Kaṭhina boundary does not follow the Law. Because of this, within the Kaṭhina boundary, there is a Natural Kaṭhina boundary. 

The signs do not necessarily need to be six or seven. For instance, in a village, most are village boundaries. If they are fixed and established and do not rely on each other, or if they are divided according to the Law, then the markers are for the Buddha's Law. The Kaṭhina signs rely on themselves. Afterwards, one marker, once it receives the Kaṭhina, if it rises to refuse the Law, it is the Kaṭhina marker. 

Within the curves, one follows the "Bucket Kaṭhina Boundary" and trusts it. Secondly, following the Law, one trusts the Kaṭhina boundary. Because of this boundary Law, within the two, a natural faith arises. The power of the two boundaries is divided; each boundary naturally has a Kaṭhina robe boundary. Because the exterior place does not follow the Law's modification, there is power.

If it is not according to the Law, it is the "Correct Kaṭhina." This "Surging Shape" below creates the Kaṭhina robe markers. Below it creates the Law Kaṭhina, which is also a flowing robe. The judgment of the flow is exhausted by the teaching robe's minimal division. Facing the "Correct Kaṭhina," the Vinaya calls it the "Fixed Kaṭhina." Following the Law provides the strength of the Kaṭhina robe. 

The **Natural Kaṭhina Robe** has "Bridge Stones" upon which the strength is divided. There is an explanation of the markers, as there were errors previously. 
**Question:** Regarding the strength of the Natural Kaṭhina land? 
**Answer:** The robe can be separated like a breast-child <note>Meaning it can be legally separated from the monk's person</note>. If one seeks the division of strength, it is the restricted Law outside the village markers. If that village is not a village, the land outside the markers where the strength is divided is where the "Heart-Governing Stone" is located. The **Kaṭhina Stone Boundary** is a type of stone boundary.

<header>On the Calculation of Planets</header>

> Thus, through the comforts of the latitude and co-latitude,
> and through hundreds of variations of the amplitude and other factors,
> there arise infinite variations of the co-latitude and its associates. || 29 ||

This is stated to demonstrate the many methods available.
### Here ends the section on the variations of the Sine of Co-latitude, Sine of Latitude, and Amplitude.

->Exposition in the Vernacular<-

In this manner, there are 63 variations of the <term>Sine of Latitude (Akshajya)</term> <note>The sine of the terrestrial latitude of the observer</note> and the <term>Sine of Co-latitude (Lambajya)</term> <note>The sine of the angle complementary to the latitude</note>. Furthermore, due to the variations in <term>Amplitude (Agra)</term> <note>The distance of the rising sun from the east point on the horizon</note> and other factors, there are infinite variations of the co-latitude and related values.

->Mathematical Rationale<-

By the method of "The Radius multiplied separately by the base and the perpendicular..." and so forth, the Sine of Co-latitude and Sine of Latitude are established in seven ways. Then, by taking each form of the Sine of Co-latitude and Sine of Latitude through the method of "The Sine of Latitude multiplied by the perpendicular and divided by the base..." and so forth, there are forty-nine (49) variations. Adding the previously mentioned seven variations makes fifty-six. Finally, by the method of "The square root of the difference of the squares of the sides..." there are seven more variations; thus, there are sixty-three variations of the Sine of Latitude and Sine of Co-latitude. || 29 ||

Now, wishing to calculate the shadow by determining the directions, the author first describes the calculation of the <term>Corner Gnomon (Kona-Shanku)</term> <note>The altitude of the sun when it is in the intermediate directions, such as Northeast or Southwest</note>.

> Subtract twice the square of the Amplitude from the square of the Radius <insert>118,198,444</insert> <note>The square of the standard radius 10,800</note>; the square root of that is the Corner Gnomon. The result should be repeatedly added to the Amplitude if it is North, or subtracted if it is South, to find the result. || 30 ||

( तीसरा हेतु ) अपनी जातिमें अवस्थित रहनेसे भी ( द्रव्य ) प्रधान है जैसे जो पार्थिव द्रव्य है वह सर्व अवस्थामें पार्थिवही रहता है अन्यभावको प्राप्त नहीं होता ( अर्थात् जो पार्थिव द्रव्य है वह पार्थिव ही रहता है और कभी आप्य, तैजस आदि नहीं होता ) इसी प्रकार शेष आप्य, तैजस, वायवीय और नाभस आदिको जानना कि ये भी अपनी २ जातिसे पृथक् नहीं होते ॥ ३ ॥ ( चौथा हेतु ) पांचों इन्द्रियोंद्वारा ग्रहण होनेसे भी ( द्रव्यही ) प्रधान है क्यों कि द्रव्यही पांचों इंद्रियों ( श्रोत्र, त्वचा, नेत्र, जिह्वा और घ्राण ) इनसे ग्रहण किया जा सकता है । और, रसादिक पांचों इंद्रियोंसे ग्रहण नहीं किये जा सकते ( केवल एक रसना इंद्रियसे रसका ग्रहण होता है इत्यादि ) ॥ ४ ॥ ( पांचवां हेतु ) द्रव्य सर्व रसादिक आश्रय स्थान होनेसे भी ( द्रव्य ) प्रधान है कि द्रव्य स्वतंत्र है और रस गुण वीर्य विपाकादि सर्व द्रव्यके आश्रयभूत ( अधीन ) हैं ॥ ५ ॥

"आरंभसामर्थ्याच्च" द्रव्याश्रित आरंभ यथा विदारिगंधादिकमाहृत्य संक्षुद्य विपचेदित्येवमादिषु न रसादिष्वारंभैः ॥ ६ ॥
"शास्त्रप्रामाण्याच्च" शास्त्रे हि द्रव्यं प्रधानमुपदेशे हि योगानां यथा मातुलुंगाग्निमंथौ चेति न रसाद्य उपदिश्यंते ॥ ७ ॥

( छठा हेतु ) द्रव्यमें आरम्भका सामर्थ्य होनेसे भी ( द्रव्य ) प्रधान है क्योंकि क्रियाका आरंभ द्रव्यके आश्रय ( अर्थात् अधीन ) है । जैसे विदारीगंधा ( शालपर्णी ) आदिको लाकर कूटे और फिर पकावे इत्यादि सर्व क्रियाओंका आरंभ द्रव्यमेंही होता है रसादिकमें किसी क्रियाकाभी आरम्भ नहीं हो सकता ॥ ६ ॥ ( सातवां हेतु ) शास्त्रके प्रमाणोंसे भी ( द्रव्य ) प्रधान है क्यों कि शास्त्रमें भी द्रव्यही प्रधान माना गया है । जैसे योगों ( नुस्खों ) के उपदेशमें मातुलुंग ( नींबू ) तथा अग्निमंथ ( अरनी ) इत्यादि द्रव्योंहीका उपदेश किया गया है कुछ रसादिक उपदेश कहीं किसी योगमें प्राप्त नहीं किया ॥ ७ ॥

"क्रमापेक्षितत्वाच्च रसादीनां" रसादयो हि द्रव्यक्रममपेक्षंते तथा तरुणे तरुणाः संपूर्णे संपूर्णा इति ॥ ८ ॥ "एकदेशसाध्यत्वाच्च द्रव्याणाम्" एकदेशनापि व्याधयः साध्यंते यथा महावृक्षक्षीरेणेति तस्माद्रव्यं प्रधानम् ॥ ९ ॥

( आठवां हेतु ) रसादिकोंकी द्रव्योंमें क्रमापेक्षा होनेसे भी ( द्रव्य ) प्रधान है अर्थात् रसादि द्रव्यके क्रमकी अपेक्षा करते हुए रहते हैं । जैसे तरुण पदार्थमें

(Third reason): Because it remains in its own nature. For example, a terrestrial substance remains terrestrial in all conditions and does not change into something else. Similarly, understand that substances of water, fire, air, and ether also do not deviate from their own nature. 3. (Fourth reason): Because it is perceived by the five senses. The substance is perceived by the ears, skin, eyes, tongue, and nose. Tastes and qualities cannot be perceived by all five senses. 4. (Fifth reason): Because the substance is the support. The substance is independent, whereas tastes, qualities, potencies, and post-digestive transformations all rely upon the substance. 5.

"Because of the capacity for action." Actions are rooted in the substance. For instance, collecting Vidārīgandhā, pounding it, and cooking it—all these actions are rooted in the substance, not in the tastes. 6. "Because of the authority of the scriptures." In the scriptures, the substance is considered primary. In the instructions for formulas, such as for the citron (<term>mātuluṅga</term>) and the <term>agnimantha</term>, the substances are taught, not just the tastes. 7.

"Because the tastes depend on the sequence of the substance." Tastes depend on the condition of the substance. For example, in a young substance, the tastes are young; in a mature one, they are mature. 8. "Because diseases can be cured by a part of the substance." Diseases can be cured even by a portion of the substance, such as the latex of the <term>mahāvṛkṣa</term> <gloss>spurge tree</gloss>. Thus, the substance is primary. 9.

The definition of a substance is that which possesses action and qualities and is the inherent cause. 10.

<meta>This page continues the technical instructions for Kabbalistic unifications (Yihudim), specifically focusing on the transitions between the Sephirot of Understanding (Binah) and Sovereignty (Malkhut) during the Sabbath rituals.</meta>

<note>A small decorative flourish in red ink, resembling an X or a cross, is located at the top center of the page.</note>

Vessels of the worlds, phylacteries <term>Tefillin: Ritual leather boxes containing Torah verses, worn during prayer to bind the mind and heart to the Divine.</term>, five vessels of Understanding <term>Binah: The third Sephirah on the Tree of Life, representing the Divine Mother or the faculty of analytical reasoning.</term>, Jacob <term>Ya'akov: In Kabbalistic thought, the patriarch Jacob often represents the Sephirah of Tiferet, the central point of harmony.</term>. He shall perform this unification <term>Yihud: A meditative practice of "unifying" divine names to repair spiritual channels.</term> in holiness and in holiness.

Sabbath eve, the afternoon prayer <term>Minchah: The afternoon prayer service, which holds significant mystical weight on the Sabbath as a time of divine favor.</term>, after he prays [the level of] Understanding over Kindness <term>Chesed: The Sephirah representing expansive love and benevolence.</term>, "Holy," and "You are..." 

to them, Understanding. And he prays the Small Rectification <term>Tikkun: An act of spiritual repair or restoration.</term> in Understanding, and afterwards in Sovereignty <term>Malkhut: The lowest Sephirah, representing the physical realm and the feminine aspect of the Divine Presence.</term>. 

Jacob, the Lord, Understanding, there upon the points of Understanding and in the soul <term>Neshamah: The higher level of the human soul associated with the intellect and the divine spark.</term>. And how good is the Ancient One <term>Atik: Referring to Atika Kadisha, the most hidden and primordial aspect of the Divine.</term>. 

In the afternoon prayers, and afterwards he shall repeat twenty [invocations of] Merciful Ones and his son, an examination, and afterwards 

MUTAL **Mazpaz** <note>original: "מצפץ". A common Kabbalistic cipher for the Tetragrammaton (YHWH) using the Atbash system, where the first letter is swapped with the last.</note>, from the mouth of **HaNetz**, from the flesh... 

**Mudash**. The secret in the rectification of the verse of His Name. He shall focus his intention <term>Kavannah: The meditative focus or mental directedness required during prayer or ritual acts.</term> on twenty of the 160 names. 

And names and small, medium, and large letters in the mouth, 160. And he shall focus his intention 

to read that which is spread out, and spread within it are rest and repose. And we have heard, and "accept the face of..." 

And this is regarding the Sabbath. And on the second day, a hint of 164, the "sling" of a bird, it is Esau <note>original: "עשוא". Esau often represents the forces of judgment or the "Other Side" in Kabbalistic literature.</note>.

The Name [YHWH] in the examination within it and Sovereignty. And "Blessed be the white one in its branch," the existences... 

Mercies for the standing of Kindnesses, 360, Understanding to Kindness, return from... 

In Gematria <term>Gematria: A system where Hebrew letters are assigned numerical values to find deeper meanings between words.</term>, the Name [YHWH] and "I Will Be" [Ehyeh]. Dew [Tal, value 39], ... Yod He Vav ... water ...

In Gematria: Yod, Yod-He, Yod-He-Vav, Yod-He-Vav-He. <note>This represents the progressive unfolding of the four-letter Name of God, used to draw divine energy down through the levels of reality.</note> 

Explanation: My son, the general name is Aleph-He-Yod-He. And there are ten letters [with a value of] 173. 

The Name in Gematria is 30 times with ... Yod-He-Vav-He ... 

And the rest of the letters are 160 until seven, he shall rectify forever for the understanding of the son. And so is the secret 

Yod-He-Vav-He. And the number 160 is all that enters ... read upon ... and "Holy." 

As in ... read until 3. And in this: Y, YH, YHV, YHVH. My son, until the reading of 87. 

And there he shall focus his intention on the Name of [45] Yod-He-Vav-He ... regarding the Shema <term>Shema: The central declaration of Jewish faith: "Hear, O Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord is One."</term>.

<summary>This page details specific meditative intentions and numerical permutations of Divine Names used during the Sabbath afternoon prayers. It emphasizes the transition between the intellectual realm of Understanding and the physical realm of Sovereignty.</summary>

### Rectification of the Prostrate <term>Tikun ha-Mishtaḥeh</term> <gloss>Rectification of the Prostrate</gloss>

And these and these shall weep a great weeping <insert>like a person</insert> for whom a relative has died, and he shall say while weeping, "Woe and alas, woe and alas," etc., three times. And he shall clap his hands one upon the other, and he shall strike upon his right and left thigh and upon his head, and he shall strike his forehead upon the ground, and he shall weep and lament a great lamentation and a bitter wailing, and he shall say, "But, alas, blessed is Thy Name, living and enduring. May Thy Name be blessed forever and ever." And then the pious of this group shall be prostrate and falling upon their faces before the one who is prostrating, until they [all] prostrate. And afterward the one prostrating shall arise and bow upward until all the prostrate have bowed. And afterward all the pious of the group shall lament, and all of them fall one upon the back of the other until all the prostrate of the great one have bowed. And afterward they shall return to their place in great weeping and great wailing upward. And thus all of them every day and every Sabbath and every month upon the sanctuary and the festival of peace, in great weeping and wailing to the Holy One, blessed be He, and He shall have mercy upon them, [granting] the redemption of their soul speedily, amen. And all those things written by the hand of Daniel, all of them shall be fulfilled. And they shall pray and weep before the Creator of the world and shall say, "May it be Thy will before Thee that Thou have mercy upon us and redeem us from this bitter exile by the merit of our holy fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, peace be upon them, and the merit of Moses and Aaron and David and Solomon, and the merit of all the righteous and the pious and the innocent and the good deeds that were in this world." And they shall be there for three days in that day, and this rectification they perform always and every Sabbath and festival. And every person shall say in great weeping and great wailing and shall say, "When shall we merit to see the building of the Holy Temple speedily in our days, amen."

And these are three things that Mordecai occupied himself with at that time in the garments of holiness. But here, because of the decree, he wore black garments, and the dust that the cantor gave—to be dressed in ashes in place of the white garment—with Mordecai, with, and so in place of the turban, they gave ashes. And Mordecai went out into the middle of the city and cried a great and bitter cry. And he cried, "Why this?" And he cried a great and bitter cry—the cantor teaches that whoever keeps the commandment of the garments, such as Mordecai, who cried a great and bitter cry and merited the kingdom. And "Mordecai went out"—this [contains] reasons for what Queen Esther asked of Mordecai, he sealed the holiness himself, and the kingdom praises him. And the names of the seven who are liable are remembered; we must mention them before the third is liable. And of this, the honor of the King of the King is mentioned, and this is his kingdom. He sealed the holy King, for the Holy One, blessed be He, called to him alone until he returns to correct it. He returned and called him, "Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a man of Benjamin." And this is the calling that did not change for him, and he was crying a great cry of Torah, and a bitter [cry] of the Divine Presence below.

### "And he came as far as before the King’s gate, for no one might come inside the King’s gate in sackcloth."

<margin></margin>
And he came as far as before the King's gate; he bought
at the King's gate, a vessel to save
</margin>

Here are the places of our vision, and already the intention of this was for Mordecai's comfort, that he had to come in the evening and the Sabbath before the King's gate. He knew that one may not come inside the King's gate in a sackcloth garment, but he had no other place to go, because they fulfilled the kindness to strive and appease the places in his merit with sackcloth, fasting, and prayer. And therefore he wore the sackcloth and cried, in the evening they informed Mordecai, to all [the more] so that they would call the little one of the answer to Mordecai, the kindnesses of prayer.

### "And in every province and province, wherever the King’s command and his law arrived, there was great mourning among the Jews, and fasting, and weeping, and lamenting; sackcloth and ashes were spread for many."

<margin></margin>
And in every province and province, the honor of our King, [His] mercy upon us
</margin>

For it was not the custom of the matter that the Jews, in all the places where the King’s command and his law arrived, [would have] sackcloth and ashes spread for many. The cantor explains the word "many," the cantor says that they were [those] who already gave him voices, that this decree was a kindness alone for them to merit them. Kindness, it is possible that it would be a garment, that they were doing kindness in the exile of the wicked, and many for them [like] these. What Mordecai cried, of the cantor, the cantor ties, [the] cantor Isaac, more, that there would be garments, cantor, and the revelation of His power, and the King's will. And this is for the [forty-nine] receiving of faces. And the Holy One, blessed be He, alone, kindness—sackcloth and ashes is not possible except for their greatness, the cantor, to the Temple and to the synagogue.

<margin>The Intellect 2</margin>
One of them, which is mentioned here, is that the Necessary Being <term>Wajib al-Wujud</term> possesses everything required for its influence on the effect. Since its state is ordered, multiplicity necessarily follows in the intellects that follow. It is appropriate to say that the Necessary Being in its uniqueness is the complete cause for the first effect. If it required something else, if that thing were accompanying it, it would be an additional attribute to its essence, which contradicts their premise. If it were separate from it, it would be a possible being in need of an agent, since we assumed it is an effect. The intellects are also generally ordered in the influence of some upon others, because everything possible for them is actually attained by them. Otherwise, there would be a temporal event <term>hadith</term> among them, and every temporal event is preceded by matter, as previously mentioned. Thus, the intellects would be concurrent with the material temporal event by its materiality, and this would lead to their termination. This is because the effect must exist when its complete cause exists. It can also be argued that if the intellect were a temporal event, it would be material, because every temporal event is preceded by matter. As for their being post-eternal, it is because if any of them were to perish, something essential to their existence would be removed. Then the remaining intellects or some of them would be susceptible to change and temporal events. This is because the matter considered in the existence of each of them is the differentiation from the essence <margin>meaning in its essence</margin> of the self. These are states accompanying the essence of the cause. **Section** on

->The manner of the mediation of the Intellects between the Creator, the Exalted, and<-
->The corporeal world. It has been established that the Necessary Being is One, and its<-
->First effect is the Pure Intellect. The celestial spheres are effects of the Intellects.<-

<margin>Principles</margin>
However, the spheres are effects of the intellects in which there is multiplicity. Therefore, they must be multiple because we have clarified that from the One, only one can issue. The intellect from which the Greatest Sphere <term>al-Falak al-A'zam</term> <gloss>the Empyrean or outermost heaven</gloss> issues contains multiplicity. But this multiplicity is not by virtue of its issuance from the Necessary Being. If the multiplicity in it were such that it issued from the Necessary, it would necessitate the issuance of multiplicity from the One. Rather, it is by virtue of its having an essence <term>mahiya</term>.

<summary>This page explains why the First Intellect must be eternal, as the Necessary Being's causality is complete and unchanging. It also introduces the problem of how multiplicity (the many spheres) arises from a single God, suggesting the First Intellect contains internal multiplicity due to its essence.</summary>

<header>فص حكمة علوية في كلمة موسوية</header>

كان رسول الله، صلى الله عليه وسلم، يبرز بنفسه للمطر إذا نزل ويكشف رأسه له حتى يصيب منه ويقول: إنه حديث عهد بربه. فانظر إلى هذه المعرفة بالله من هذا النبي ما أجلها وما أعلاها وأوضحها. فقد سخر المطر أفضل البشر لقربه من ربه فكان مثل الرسول الذي ينزل بالوحي عليه، فدعاه بالحال بذاته فبرز إليه ليصيب منه ما أتاه به من ربه فلو لا ما حصلت له منه <gloss>١</gloss> الفائدة الإلهية بما أصاب منه، ما برز بنفسه إليه. فهذه رسالة ماء جعل الله منه ﴿وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ﴾ (الأنبياء: ٣٠) فافهم.

وأما حكمة إلقائه في التابوت ورميه في اليم، فالتابوت ناسوته، واليم ما حصل له من العلم بواسطة هذا الجسم مما أعطته القوة النظرية الفكرية والقوى الحسية والخيالية التي لا يكون شيء منها ولا من أمثالها لهذه <gloss>٢</gloss> النفس الإنسانية إلا بوجود [١٣٨ الف] هذا الجسم العنصري. فلما حصلت النفس في هذا الجسم وأمرت بالتصرف فيه وتدبيره، جعل الله لها هذه القوى آلات <gloss>٣</gloss> يتوصل بها إلى ما أراده الله منها في تدبير هذا التابوت الذي فيه سكينة الرب.

فرمى به في اليم ليحصل بهذه القوى على فنون العلم فأعلمه بذلك أنه وإن كان الروح المدبر له هو الملك، فإنه لا يدبره إلا به. فأصحبه هذه القوى الكائنة في هذا الناسوت الذي عبر عنه بالتابوت في باب الإشارات والحكم.

كذلك تدبير الحق العالم ما دبره إلا به أو بصورته، فما دبره إلا به كتوقف الولد على إيجاد الوالد، والمسببات على أسبابها، والمشروطات على شروطها، والمعلولات على عللها، والمدلولات على أدلتها، والمحققان على حقائقها. وكل ذلك من العالم وهو تدبير الحق فيه. فما دبره إلا به. وأما قولنا أو بصورته، أعنى صورة العالم، فأعنى به الأسماء الحسنى والصفات العلى التي تسمى الحق بها واتصف بها. فما وصل إلينا اسم تسمى به إلا وجدنا معنى ذلك الاسم وروحه في العالم. فما دبر العالم أيضا إلا بصورة العالم.

ولذلك قال في خلق آدم الذي هو البرنامج الجامع لنعوت الحضرة الإلهية التي هي الذات والصفات والأفعال: «إن الله خلق آدم على صورته.» وليست صورته سوى الحضرة الإلهية. فأوجد <gloss>٤</gloss> في هذا المختصر الشريف الذي هو الإنسان الكامل جميع الأسماء الإلهية وحقائق ما خرج عنه في العالم الكبير المنفصل، وجعله روحا

<header>### Gem of Lofty Wisdom in the Word of Moses</header>

The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, used to go out into the rain when it fell and uncover his head to it so that it would touch him. He would say: "It has newly come from its Lord." Look at this knowledge of God from this Prophet; how majestic, high, and clear it is! The rain subjugated the best of humanity because of its proximity to its Lord. It was like the Messenger to whom revelation descends. It called him through its state and essence, so he went out to it to receive the divine benefit it brought from his Lord. Had he not obtained a divine benefit from it touching him, he would not have gone out to it. This is the message of the water from which God made "every living thing" <note>Quran 21:30</note>. Understand this.

As for the wisdom of him being placed in the ark and cast into the river, the ark represents his <term>nasut</term> <gloss>human nature or physical body</gloss>. The river <note>original: "al-yamm"</note> represents the knowledge he obtained by means of this body. This includes what was given to him by the faculties of theoretical thought, the senses, and the imagination. None of these, nor their like, would exist for this human soul without the existence of this elemental body. 

When the soul entered this body and was commanded to manage and direct it, God made these faculties tools to reach what God intended for it in the management of this ark, within which lies the tranquility of the Lord. He was cast into the river so that he might obtain the various branches of knowledge through these faculties. Through this, He informed him that even though the spirit managing him is the king, it can only manage him through these faculties. He accompanied him with these powers existing in this human nature, which was expressed as the "ark" in the language of symbols and wisdom.

Similarly, the management of the Truth <note>original: "al-Haqq"</note> over the world is only done through the world, or through its image. He only manages it through itself, just as a child depends on the existence of a parent, effects depend on their causes, conditions on their prerequisites, results on their premises, and proofs on their evidence. All of this is part of the world, and it is the management of the Truth within it. He only manages it through it. 

When we say "or through its image," meaning the image of the world, I mean the Beautiful Names and Lofty Attributes by which the Truth named Himself and with which He is described. Every name by which He is called has a meaning and a spirit that we find within the world. Therefore, the world is also managed only through the image of the world.

For this reason, He said regarding the creation of Adam, who is the comprehensive program of the descriptions of the Divine Presence—which are the Essence, Attributes, and Acts: "God created Adam in His image." His image is nothing other than the Divine Presence. He placed within this noble summary, which is the Perfect Human <note>original: "al-Insan al-Kamil"</note>, all the divine names and the realities of everything that exists outside him in the great, separate world. He made him a spirit...

translation:
...its construction is truly on the <term>ḍammah</term>, not on a hidden <term>fatḥah</term>. At that time, his words are clearly in line with the first possibility... contrary to the apparent text of the manuscript. If it is so, then it should be interpreted accordingly here and in what preceded. Reflect with fairness.

<insert>His saying</insert> "according to al-Kisāʾī": he only attributed the <term>ḍammah</term> for the <term>Lām</term> to the school of al-Kisāʾī because he expressed it using the term "jussive" <term>jazm</term>, which is one of the titles of declension <term>iʿrāb</term>. No one is followed in that except those who say it is declinable, namely al-Kisāʾī and those who followed him. It is not appropriate to carry his words to a remote school; rather, they should be carried to a school that eases the additions... or it is said that the meaning of his saying "jussive" is to be treated like a jussive. This is supported by the author's previous saying: "the verbs are three." He specifically mentioned the <term>ḍammah</term> for al-Kisāʾī because he is the Imam of the people of Kufa.

<insert>His saying</insert> "to lighten": i.e., to lighten the pronunciation of it. <insert>His saying</insert> "for fear of confusion with the sound-ending present-tense verb in the state of pause." <insert>His saying</insert> "at the need for it": in that the letter after the present-tense prefix is still <term>sākin</term>, as illustrated: the <term>Ḍād</term> in "he strikes" <term>yaḍribu</term> is still, so it is brought [the helper vowel] to reach the pronunciation of the still letter. The letter after the present-tense prefix was not moved... out of fear of two still letters meeting. If that <term>Hamzah</term> [of connection] is not needed, it is not brought, such as when the letter after the present-tense prefix is moving <term>mutaḥarrik</term>, like "he rolls" <term>yudaḥriju</term>...

<column-break/>

The consideration of it being "moving" is by its literal form, not its underlying estimation. Even if it is moving literally but still in estimation—such as "stand" <term>qum</term> and "sell" <term>biʿ</term>—for their origin is "taqūmu" and "tabīʿu"... you say "qum" and "biʿ".

<insert>His saying</insert> "built on stillness": i.e., on the principle in verbs and indeclinability. The principle in verbs is indeclinability, and the principle in indeclinability is stillness <term>sukūn</term>, so one does not ask for their cause. The closest to literal stillness is like "invade" <term>ughzu</term>, and the estimated stillness is like "invade" <term>ughzū</term>, "be angry," and "be strong"... 

If the "Nūn of women" <term>nūn al-niswah</term> is attached, it is built on stillness. If the commentator had said: "The command <term>amr</term> according to Sibawayh is built on what its present-tense is apocopated with, as long as it is not attached to the Nūn of women, otherwise it is built on stillness, or the Nūn of Emphasis, otherwise it is built on the fatḥah like the present-tense in both," it would have been more specific and comprehensive.

<insert>His saying</insert> "and on its deletion at the end if it is a weak-ending verb": i.e., if it is not attached to the <term>Alif</term> of duality, the <term>Wāw</term> of the group, the <term>Yā</term> of the address, the <term>Nūn</term> of women, or a directly attached <term>Nūn</term> of Emphasis. If those are joined to it, then in things... as he ruled by his saying: "or on its deletion and the Nūn." But he did not mention the ruling of the <term>Nūn</term> of women and the <term>Nūn</term> of Emphasis, which is known from what preceded: that with the first it is built on stillness, like "strike ye [fem.]," "invade ye," "fear ye," and "throw ye"; and with the second it is built on the <term>fatḥah</term>, like "invade [thou] indeed," "fear indeed," and "throw indeed."

<insert>His saying</insert> "The four extras": "extras" <term>zawāʾid</term> is the plural of "extra" <term>zāʾidah</term>...

...requested permission from her master, was ordained, and through great diligence manifested the fruit of Arhatship. She became the foremost among the nuns who analyze the Sutras.

Again, while the Blessed One was staying in Anathapindada's garden <note>Jetavana</note>, a sea captain named Ocean-Born <note>original: "Rgya mtsho skyes"</note> went to sea with a retinue of five hundred merchants. They were overtaken by the "Black Ogre Wind" <note>a storm</note> and became terrified and exhausted. The captain prayed to the six teachers, but the boat was still tossed by the wind. Other merchants cried out and prayed to a thousand gods like Gulang, Varuna <note>original: "Chu lha"</note>, and Kubera, but no one provided refuge.

Then a lay practitioner <note>original: "Dge bsnyen"</note> said, "The six teachers and other gods can do nothing for you. Go for refuge from your heart to the Buddha, the Blessed One, who is a manifest god; he will be your refuge." Then the merchants with one voice went for refuge to the Buddha.

The Blessed One, staying in Jetavana, knew this. He radiated light like the color of gold, brighter than a thousand suns, and illuminated all the merchants. He also radiated the light of loving-kindness, cultivated for a thousand eons, which gave them relief and turned back the "Black Ogre Wind." Then those merchants returned from the sea without harm. 

When they requested an invitation for the midday meal, he accepted by remaining silent. Then that householder went to his home, and that night he prepared many kinds of excellent food and drink. Rising early in the morning, he arranged the seating and sent word that it was time for the meal. The Blessed One, together with the community of monks, went to the householder's dining hall. 

When the boy <note>the hunchback mentioned on the next page</note> saw the Blessed One from a distance, great joy arose in him. With a manner of intense respect, he rose from his chair. The moment he rose from the chair, his hunched back became straight, just as it was before. Then, with even greater joy, he prostrated and touched the feet of the Buddha, saying, "The Blessed One has performed a difficult task for me; the Sugata has performed a difficult task for me."

Then the Blessed One sat upon the seat arranged in the center of the Sangha. The householder served whatever excellent food and drink they desired. After the meal was finished, the householder and his retinue sat before the Blessed One to listen to the Dharma. To them, he taught the Dharma according to their faculties...

May all sentient beings attain unsurpassed enlightenment through these virtues, which are gathered and explained according to the roots of virtue taught in the examples of the wish-fulfilling tree, representing the intent of the great teacher’s <term>tsoklam</term> <gloss>path of accumulation</gloss> scripture. May all the roots of virtue of sentient beings in the three realms be gathered into one and dedicated together with my own roots of virtue. May these dedicated virtues purify all the obscurations of all sentient beings, and may the entire collection of merit be perfected. Then, may one encounter the dedication of the roots of virtue of the Great Vehicle <term>Mahayana</term>. Then, may one encounter the dedication of the roots of virtue of the Great Vehicle. May one attain non-abiding <term>nirvana</term> <gloss>liberation beyond sorrow</gloss>. Then, through the inexhaustible blessings of the roots of virtue of the Great Vehicle, may all the desires in the minds of all sentient beings be completely fulfilled. This dedication of the roots of virtue, which points to the one, should be dedicated for the sake of being the foundation for all sentient beings.

<vocab>རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་ (Perfect Buddha), སྤྲུལ་པའི་མཐུ་ (Power of emanation), སྒྲིབ་པ་ (Obscurations), འཕྲིན་ལས་ (Enlightened activity), སངས་རྒྱས་ (Buddha), ཐུགས་རྗེའི་མཛད་པ་ (Compassionate activity), སྤྱན་གཟིགས་ (Avalokiteshvara), ཀུན་ཏུ་བཟང་པོ་ (Samantabhadra), བྱམས་པ་ (Maitreya), རྣམ་པར་རྒྱལ་མ་ (Ushnisha Vijaya)</vocab>
translation:
The power of the emanations of the Perfect Buddha <note>original: "Samyaksambuddha"</note> dispels all obscurations through the mere hearing of his name. He is the lamp of refuge, pervasive and limitless in his enlightened activity. He is spontaneously established as the Buddha.

Avalokiteshvara <note>original: "Chenrezig"</note> is the clear manifestation of compassionate activity. He dwells everywhere in great power. Above the high sky in front of oneself and others, he dwells, spontaneously established. Samantabhadra gazes into the expanse. He is the master of the sky. Maitreya holds the reversal of obscurations. Likewise, the hundred-fold signs <note>the Buddha's physical marks</note> are in the name of the Lord of Gods. The Noble One of Bliss is blissful, and through hearing her, one is cleared of all obscurations. The Mother, the great Goddess, works to redeem obscurations. The deity with three faces and eight hands is the body of activity. The glorious wisdom-sign, the victorious goddess, dwells in that state. She is the manifestation of the brilliant radiance of craftsmanship.
